title: Remove K Digits
description:
Given a non-negative integer represented as a string of digits `num` and an integer `k`, remove exactly `k` digits from `num` so that the resulting number is the **smallest possible**.

Return the resulting number as a string with no leading zeros (if all digits are removed or only zeros remain, return `"0"`).
constraints: num consists only of digits '0'-'9' and has no leading zeros except possibly "0" itself.
hints: Iterate through the digits left to right using a monotonic increasing stack: whenever the current digit is smaller than the stack top and k > 0, pop the larger digit and decrement k.
If k > 0 after processing all digits, pop the remaining k digits from the end of the stack, strip leading zeros, and return "0" if empty.

examples.explanation: Removing digits 4, 3, and 2 from "1432219" yields the smallest possible number "1219".
Removing the leading '1' from "10200" leaves "0200", which strips leading zeros to "200".
Removing all 2 digits from "10" leaves nothing, so return "0".
